Title: Let's Go Out Tonight
Comment: The name of the artist on this recording actually stays in my area in Glasgow-technically Paul Buchanan was never really Glaswegian .  I'm going to talk a little about Glasgow here -I lost one of my greatest friends on Easter Monday . Ironically Gordon was American but moved back to Glasgow in the late 60's-a story that was always told as being due to his parents splitting up. There's a sting in that tale. I will recount on the follow up replies. Me and Gordon met in 1982 when Glasgow was a thriving centre of cool-if that matters but him being 4 years older than me-he took me under his wing and we went to the best bars and clubs. Music was central to us-he wasn't a rock fan per se -and we gelled on The Blue Nile and I turned him onto Eitzel. We went to the football together for over 40 years and he looked after me when I really needed it and was an uniquely good person. I miss him deeply so this is for him. . I miss the Glasgow of this song too.

Title: Interpretes
Comment:
"I wanna go back to my home town
Though I know it'll never be the same"
- Joe Jackson

This is a timely round, as I am actually spending the summer with family in Midland, Michigan (USA). 

Years ago, I was home on break from university, and like many young folks I took a short-term job to make some extra money. I was part of a rotating work crew for our local public works department, doing various tasks like pouring sidewalks, filling potholes, and clearing brush.

One of my supervisors was a friendly man named Ivan. We were at lunch one day when he told a story about going to see his son play in a band opening for Neil Young. It took me a minute, but I figured out he was referring to Steve Shelley of Sonic Youth (who, by the way, is the spitting image of his father).

We've already had SY and current collaborator Bill Orcutt, so here's a track from Shelley's 2009 team-up with Chicago indie rock artists Disappears and White/Light, eventually released on Shelley's own label in 2020.

Title: Love Bird
Comment: Welcome to Snoqualmie, birthplace of Ella Raines (watch "Tall In the Saddle" with John Wayne if you ever get a chance).  Issaquah, the second town west on Interstate 90, would have given you Modest Mouse.  Instead, here's a 2017 offering from Snoqualmie local Strong Sun Moon (an acoustic world-fusion and roots group featuring Camelia Jade and Mike Antone).  The alternate choice was Mother Root, a heavy sludge/doom duo.  You're welcome.

Title: New York, Let's Do Nothing
Comment: I felt sure we’d had King Hannah before, but the spreadsheet says no. My favourite Liverpool band of recent years, an irresistible mix of Mazzy Star, Neil Young and PJ Harvey, with a fondness for chatty but surreal lyrics - shining stars in a city currently with an apparently infinite supply of bands who look and sound like The La’s (if being generous) or Cast (if being honest).

Title: Summer
Comment: These wide-open rounds seem easy at first, but give me indecision paralysis. Melbourne (Australia) has obviously produced a decent band or two, but after a while thinking through some big names, I landed on a more underground moment that still lurks in the city’s musical DNA. This is from a wondrous compilation gathering some of the strangest and spikiest output of the post-punk years from 1978-82, not all of it from Melbourne, but featuring a good number of the Little Bands from our town, a kind of musical swingers’ scene in which groups formed, performed once or twice, then vanished, before reshuffling again (complete with disposable band names like Slugfuckers, People With Chairs Up Their Noses, Thrush and the Cunts). The Take only recorded this one song, but for me it nails the spirit of the era - yelping vocals, a touch of sadism (that siren guitar!), and serious humour .

Title: Shadow (Maceo Plex Remix)
Comment:
Well, I could be one of two Portland fireflies on the list. Betcha can't guess which one I am! The past Firefly music leagues I have posted a sampler plate of the rich music scene we have here in PDX.  However, if you examine the origin of some of those, you will find some of the most well known Portland band members actually are transplants to our fair city. Finding a band whose members were born and bred here was a challenge.  

Here, we have the Chromatics, whose members are all Portland natives. Their sound is gauzy, airy, dripping in reverb, just ripe for the picking to appear on TV and movie soundtracks. This remix, by producer Maceo Plex, was intended to "pay tribute and honour the death of Twin Peaks‘ fictional character, Laura Palmer who was originally portrayed by Sherly Lee."

Portland's creative landscape continues to thrive in spite of efforts by red hats to dry out our dampness. Keep Portland Weird! (Yes, I know we that slogan was stolen from Austin).

Title: Good Life
Comment:
Iggy Pop was raised in a trailer park in my town of Ypsilanti, very close to the grocery store I shop at.  However, Memorial Day weekend in Detroit means it's time for the annual electronic music festival, now called Movement.  This year, on the Friday before the long weekend, I was lucky enough to catch a super rare-- nay, historical-- show by the Belleville Three (Techno originators Juan Atkins, Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson) in their hometown where they met as teens, Belleville, Michigan, which is next door to Ypsilanti.
It is hard now to imagine the world before EDM took it over like a gigantic, tedious octopus.  But these kids (now approaching retirement age) had the skills and vision to create something new and exciting.
Kind of a funny sidenote: 10% of the door take was donated to the Belleville High School robotics club, as befits the futuristic music.
Here is Inner City's (Kevin Saunderson  + singer Paris Grey) 1988 classic "Good Life".  Shake your booty.

Comment:
Since I can't use the ol'  "little league games in NJ and Subway sandwich" subterfuge to hide my location and identity, I might as well go all in: 

HELP are a tremendously noisy rock band from Portland OR who are best experienced live, and, as this track might suggest, their shows are very politically charged affairs. The drummer doesn't really play the drums, so much as assaults them with an over the shoulder attack (sort of visible in the looping clip on Spotify). Interestingly enough, the guitarist and singer spent time in another far more famous PDX (airport code for Portland which  is common shorthand for the city itself) band, Portugal the Man, which is pretty fascinating when you realize he had all of .... uh....  *this* ...  bottled up inside. Glad he's getting it out!

Title: Go All The Way
Comment:
In the Cleveland metro area, I'm spoiled for choices, but I get overwhelmed by options, so I decided to interpret "the town where you currently live" as narrowly as possible.

Eric Carmen grew up in my current suburb and went to the same high school my kids attend. The city held a celebration of life just after his death.

Although we had another selection from the Raspberries in the last league (and though some voters may take a dim view of repeat artists), this really is an incredible song. I could have opted for one of his later solo outings which were still expertly crafted soft rock hits, but this one is simply better. The absolutely classic opening riff foreshadows the edgy (for the time) subject matter and then transitions almost magically into the most innocent sounding and buttery smooth chorus.

There are plenty of songs with unforgettable hooks and plenty of songs with incredible songwriting, but this one comes from the much smaller pile that offers up both.

As such, their album is “Singin’ To An Empty Chair,” a nod to the  Gestalt technique invented in the 1920s. You could DIY, but results may vary. Title: Bubble Sex
Comment:
My fellow Dane might kill me for submitting this, but I think it’s time we reexamined the oeuvre of Copenhagen* native mr. Seebach. Primarily known for his somewhat naff Eurovision schlagers (though Disco Tango is a banger; this is a hill I will die on), this song is the best song Giorgio Moroder never wrote. Seebach was an early adopter of electronic music, even if he might primarily have copied trends from abroad. But you can’t deny the excellent result!

* Tommy Seebach was born in Copenhagen but lived in Frederiksberg, which is a municipality nestled entirely within the municipality of Copenhagen. Copenhageners and Frederiksbergians might debate what’s what, and what’s best, but except for tax purposes the rest of the world sees no difference.

Title: Gough
Comment:
There were reasons.  How long have you got?

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gough_Whitlam - Australia's 21st Prime Minister, serving from December 1972 to November 1975.  His full name is Edward Gough Whitlam, popularly known as Gough.  From the band's Wiki page:  According to Freedman "I loved the family names—the Smiths, the Reivers. I thought, the Whitlams, no-one's done that. I'll be able to steal all the goodwill that Australia holds in reserve for Gough Whitlam."

Stevie (who was "9 in 1972") is Stevie Plunder, one third of this incarnation of the Whitlams.  The first two Whitlams albums are more more rollicking, shambolic at times, with the back and forth between Tim Freedman (singing lead here) and Stevie.  Stevie passed in 1996, and Tim solely took the band reins to make Eternal Nightcap, their brilliant third studio album.  Gough presented them with their "Best Group" ARIA award at the 1998 ceremony.

Title: Judith
Comment:
Judith Marie Garrison suffered a devastating brain aneurysm in 1976 that left her paralyzed, a condition that remained until her death in 2003. Her son James was only 11 at the time of the incident.

Judith was a devout Southern Baptist, and kept her faith despite the hardships she endured, but her son did not share her religious beliefs.

After a brief stint in the U.S. Army, James rechristened himself as Maynard James Keenan. He would go on to write several songs referencing his mother and her condition, but none more explicit than this one.

"He did this
Took all you had and
Left you this way
Still you pray, 
Never stray, never 
Taste of the fruit
Never thought 
To question why

It’s not like you killed someone
It’s not like you drove a hateful spear into his side
Praise the one who left you broken down and paralyzed
He did it all for you"

Years later, Keenan would go on to offer a more reflective and compassionate tribute to Judith:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BMsmF7d4h5E

Title: Move With Me
Comment:
Don Cherry was a jazz trumpeter who rose to prominence as a sideman with Ornette Coleman and then went on to have a long career across several musical genres. He worked closely with his wife, visual artist Moki Cherry, who created his album covers and set designs. Theirs was an artistic family, including several children who became professional musicians.

Neneh Cherry exploded into fame with "Buffalo Stance" in 1988 and her debut solo album 'Raw Like Sushi' the following year.

"Move With Me", co-written with Cherry's husband Cameron McVey and taken from her second album 'Homebrew', is a hypnotically sensual and introspective examination of life and how the rhythms of nature and partnership intertwine.

"Motions as we move gives me
A clearer description
Than the words I string together
When I'm looking for expression
Or words I read for wisdom
As I'm searching for some answers"

Cherry's daughters Tyson and Mabel have also continued the family tradition as recording artists in the UK.

Title: Dead Meat
Comment:
I don’t believe I need to introduce Sean Ono Lennon. I’m sure entire books have been written on the family dynamic. I think Sean knows who he sounds like, and how he doesn’t. If you get past that, you could find a piece of work by someone who experienced pain as real as anyone else’s.

Sean wrote Friendly Fire after a nasty betrayal— his best friend Max had an affair with his girlfriend, and then Max died in a motorcycle accident before he could made amends. The album helped me get through a nasty betrayal back in the mid-aughts. I settled on Dead Meat for the simmering, eerie, life-is-a-circus sound and the satisfying idea that, at least sometimes, people do get what they deserve.

"At first it seems fairly plain, built around Lennon's thin voice (friendly, if lacking fire)....Yet there's more to the album, most explicitly in the spiked words -troubled, uncertain, seeking security in an impermanent world.”

Title: Dreamin' Of
Comment: “Dreamin’ Of” by Pieta Brown is a song that evokes open space. It's a soft breath more than a bold declaration. The circling acoustic guitar lays down a hushed, suspended atmosphere where every note of Pieta’s voice can linger. The song lives in that quiet space between longing and acceptance. You can hear echoes of her father, Greg Brown, in the grounded storytelling, while the emotional subtlety and poetic hush nod toward her stepmother, Iris DeMent. Pieta's songwriting and voice don’t beg for attention but like light quietly fading at dusk, their beauty is undeniable.

Title: The Songs That We Sing
Comment:
Papa: Serge Gainsbourg, the quintessential French genius/alcoholic/arsehole. 

Mama: Jane Birkin, who met Serge on the set of their film Slogan in 1968 (her at 21, him at 40, of course). 

They made an album together including the infamous “Je t'aime... moi non plus", and a few years later, Charlotte arrived - 35 years after that came 5:55, her first album as an adult (I’m glossing over the teenage “Lemon Incest” period, I can’t even). This song wears both parental influences proudly in its arrangement and her voice - weirdly devoid of French accent - but also brings an A-Team of collaborators, with Jarvis Cocker and Neil Hannon co-writing the lyrics questioning the whole business of songwriting, and Air as musical maestros.

Title: Girl on LSD - Alternate Version
Comment:
"I was really trying to hone something different for a while there, and then I felt like I'd got that out of my system and now it was time to do something a little rawer and earthier." - Tom Petty

Petty's 'Wildflowers' was originally conceived as a double album before it was hewn down to 15 tracks for its 1994 release. One of the casualties was "Girl on LSD", relegated to b-side status via the album's first single.

The humor in the song speaks for itself, but it also has an interesting history. Co-producer Rick Rubin dismisses it as a "fun throwaway... we laughed a lot in the studio thanks to this one", but Petty's daughter Adria claims her father intended it to be the closing song in the original double album sequencing. Petty himself thought enough of "Girl on LSD" to feature it in his live set as late as 2008 (https://open.spotify.com/track/6RhmiL6iRRFzdYNxIa4mw0) and likely would have included it on an expanded 'Wildflowers' he was planning in 2017 before his untimely passing.

Title: 70's Rock Must Die
Comment: Two of the nicest guys in rock history, Jello Biafra and Al Jourgensen, team up to pen a love letter to the rock legends that inspired them to create music in the first place.  I recommend following along with the lyrics as they reference iconic 70's moments such as country rock, Saturday Night Fever, Led Zep, Aerosmith, The Sex Pistols and ... um ... "collegiate boy Neil Young copy bands."

Title: Tony's Got Hot Nuts
Comment: I’m not really sure this qualifies for the round, being as it is a straightforward song about a vendor of savory treats, sold at the bargain price of ten cents a bag - not five cents - ten cents a bag.

Title: Kinema
Comment: One of my new favourite bands this year. Slow paced metronomic beats, building to a hypnotic chant. Atmospheric, beautiful.

Title: Linger On
Comment: If I was in charge Two Gallants would have been massive. For some reason I’m not in charge, and they haven’t released anything in over 10 years. This song is slow (approximately 69bpm according to google AI), and fairly long, but is a definite 7 pointer as far as I’m concerned.

Title: Starless - Abridged
Album: The Condensed 21st Century Guide To King Crimson (1969 - 2003)
Comment: "Starless" was originally conceived as the title track for the band's sixth studio album 'Starless and Bible Black' but was reworked with additions by contributing lyricist Richard Palmer-James and subsequently became the closing song on 1974's 'Red'. This "abridged" version (created for a 1991 retrospective box set) is essentially a standalone release of the song's balladic opening section, evocatively sung by vocalist/bassist John Wetton. I have always loved the melancholic imagery of the lyrics as a perfect complement to the brooding bed of intertwined guitar and saxophone... a longtime favourite and an incredible mood setter.

Title: Safe House
Comment: From my favourite album of 2024, which was written in response to the passing of Sinead O'Connor, here is a song which showcases the wonderful vocals of Shara Nova, with whom I have become a little obsessed since seeing her open for Alan Sparhawk last time he was in town.

Title: Elusive
Comment: Stumbled on this song sometime during the early days of the pandemic. It quickly became a part of my playlist that I used to calm my nerves in the worst of times. The diaphanous quality of his voice and dreamy production worked as a soothing balm. Slow down, listen, and breathe.

Title: Holocaust
Comment: I've just discovered the 'previous submissions' google sheet! Better late than never. No Big Star by the looks of it so far...

Title: Always Returning - Remastered 2005
Comment:
Imagine your mind as an open sky. Whenever a distracting thought drifts into view, don't push it away. Instead, picture it simply floating by like a wisp of vapor, allowing your attention to drift back to the safety of the music.
Feel the sensation of expansion. With each deliberate, echoing piano note, imagine a wave of calm washing over you, from the top of your crown, to your hot salty gonads, all the way down to your toes.

Title: Look Away
Comment: Ida's Elizabeth Mitchell is a co-writer on this lovely track from her debut album.  First heard her thanks to "Okay", an acoustic guitar & cello song of love and support to a friend (waterworks trigger warning).   https://tulliah.bandcamp.com/

Title: (That's How You Sing) Amazing Grace
Comment: This one is for all the lovebirds on heavy narcotics....

Title: A Universal Hello
Comment: Slooow oh and a bit long but it's very good -may be some arguments about A and An .......

Title: Loss Leader
Comment: As soon as I saw the brief for this round, I thought of Codeine - not just because they’re always in the list of bands when you look up “slowcore” (along with AMC, which I can never understand), but also because they meant a lot to me, back in the day. They weren’t just slow, they stripped everything back to just a few notes and drumbeats, with plenty of space in-between - even the lyrics circled around themes of loss and lack and absence. Yes, slowcore is also sadcore. I guess I was a sadcore youth. But I’m better now. ALL BETTER *laughcries*

Title: Red Bird Morning
Comment: There are many ways to approach this round. But I knew that I did not want slow as to be comatose. I also wished to choose something newer to me, and perhaps new to you. I find this rather sad and lovely. I had an aunt who swore her departed mother kept coming back to her in the form of a cardinal— turns out many folks believe those we have lost come back as red birds to visit us.

Title: Chariot
Comment: Well the strategy of going with 90's era stuff hasn't resulted in the avalanche of points I was expecting so let's try to teach the old dog(s) some new trick(s) with this 2024 cut from an upstate(ish) NY duo.  You've got something in your pocket?

Title: Beams
Comment: Swedish band Tape makes sort of acoustic electronic music. It sounds a bit like very brief early 70’s prog rock instrumentals except it doesn’t. But they are always slow and beautiful.

Title: Crystal Silence - Previously Unissued
Comment: I know what you’re thinking, “Did this clown just post a 7:46 slow jazz song?” Yes. Yes I did. Stan Getz teams up with Chic Corea for a beautiful version of Corea’s song. The electric piano effect is almost Wurlitzer like and completely fascinating to me. The song drifts along on the piano as Stan plays the melody with reverence and it seems a little sorrow. It’s a beautiful piece of music and I hope you can take some slow deep breaths and let it wash over your brain.

Title: Listen, The Snow Is Falling
Comment: Slowcore from Galaxie 500. A band I was obsessed with in my first year at University. Dubbed out shoegaze/dream pop slowed down and drown in a hazy bath of reverb of Spaceman 3 & The Velvet Underground guitars. When I first heard this I didn't know it was a cover as someone had taped me the LP. A C90 I no-longer own, I wish I did it had a lovely hand drawn cover, with This Is Our Music on one side and Cowboy Junkies Trinity Sessions on the other. Two records I still love today. A Sunday morning coming down tape that help ease those hangovers.

Title: My Old Friend the Blues
Comment: One from the old days, slow pace but Eddie's voice guides one through it smoothly. Saw her support Mark on a youtube video somewhere.

Title: Song for Zula
Comment: Won’t be the slowest song submitted this week, but it plods along hypnotically and still feels shorter than it is. Among the best I’ve found for an introspective late night drive, or the stillness after a party has burned out. There’s just enough speed here to pull you in as you space out. If you are listening in the cold light of day, try again in the dark after a long day… or a great day.

Title: Lose Me On the Way
Comment:
(Listed incorrectly on Spotify - this is actually Around My Smile). 

Hope Sandoval does not do anything quickly. I reckon I could potentially even beat her in the sports day parents’ race. This is one of her slowest and best.

Title: Change - 2005 Digital Remaster
Comment: “change” in this song very is much an instruction - a command even. yeah we had kj once before but that was misplacing them in the goth round so it doesn’t count right?

Title: Pick up the Phone
Comment:
Is this very familiar, I wondered? Let’s split you into two groups: Do you know this song? If No, proceed to intro 1. If Yes, skip to intro 2.

1. The Notwist’s melding of indie rock and skittery electronic-acoustic sounds blew up fairly big with this album back in 2002. They’re originally from (adopts comedy German accent) Weilheim in Oberbayern, a little Bavarian town right down at the southern end of the country, but are now based in Munich. Those who like to understand the lyrics will be pleased to hear that they share their wistful thoughts in English. Isn’t it awesome?

2. Can you believe this is 24 years old already? Ah, those were the days. In centuries past, nostalgia was considered an illness, treated with leeches or morphine. In modern times, we can just listen to songs from back when we were actually young, not just “young at heart”. Isn’t it awesome?

Title: Get In Line
Comment: Lots of options in their catalog like "Glitter Us", "Tell Someone Who Gives A Fuck", "Write What You Know", "Always Look For the Bad in People", and more.  Chose this for its minor key sunny undercurrent.  Wayne Connolly's production help is noticeable. https://thefauves.com/ and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fauves_(band)

Title: Turn It On
Comment: I feel like we need an antidote after that last round and there are few songs in my catalog that trigger movement quicker than this one.  Plus, for this theme Anjali's command will be a self-filling prophecy.

Title: Throw Your Arms Around Me
Comment:
Hunters & Collectors originally released this paean to the pure joys (and sometimes fleeting nature) of human connection as a one-off single in 1984 before re-recording it for their 'Human Frailty' album.

The song features one of my all-time favorite pop music choruses:

"You will make me call your name
And I'll shout it to the blue summer sky
We may never meet again
So shed your skin and let's get started
And you will throw your arms around me"

Described by one writer as "Australia’s secular hymn", this one goes out to Alister Shew, who I'm sure has never heard the song before today.

Title: Jean, Bring the Flowers
Comment:
“Jean, Bring the Flowers” is a bright little earworm that caught me off guard when  I heard it in a pub. I thought it was some lost Lloyd Cole track. It wasn’t. It was Pale Lights.

Singer/Songwriter Phil Sutton drove the band’s crisp, jangly indie pop. Sadly, they’re no more.

This is music for dusty record shops on rainy Sundays.

Jean really had one job—bring the flowers.

Title: Add This Song
Comment: No Gus Gus in the league yet? Time to rectify! I always liked the indie electronica of Icelandic Gus Gus. So add this song! Or even better add some points.

Title: Let Your Dog Tooth Grow
Comment: First submission for the Orielles. They’ve got progressively more challenging (although still very good) through the course of their four albums, but this is one from their more accessible debut, with a slightly confusing instruction.

Title: Don't Start Now
Comment: I can see you rolling your eyes but straightforward disco music for pre-teens this is not. When the bass kicks in with a growl after 9 seconds, and then goes on to dance around this banger in a manner that is just irresistible, you won't be responsible for your actions.

Title: Spit It Out
Comment: Let's have a bit of moody, yet incredibly danceable, synth-pop this week. This track could work in almost any setting as long as the night is not too young. Grit and fuzz, very hooky, and tons of energy. Volume up!

Title: Pipe Down!
Artist(s): Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs

Title: Twist the Knife
Comment: There's no better voice with which to illustrate the heart wrenching grandeur of heartbreak, and she balances both the power and the bleakness of the whole thing delightfully on this little number, which ultimately is reassuring and comforting as a jam and peanut butter sandwich.

Title: Let My People Go
Album: You Must Be Certain Of The Devil
Comment: An acquired taste, perhaps, but I adore everything she does—even the completely bonkers, screaming stuff. This is her reworking of Go Down Moses, written in response to her brother's death from AIDS.

Title: Feast On My Heart - Remastered
Comment:
Pylon came out of the same Athens, Georgia, USA scene as REM and the B-52s, and were constantly championed by those bands.

I personally cannot imagine asking someone to feast on my heart, not least for fear they would feel peckish later and then where would we be?  Anyway, that surely can't be the start of a healthy relationship.  But I'd give her what she's asking for, if I were you.

Title: Join in the Chant
Comment: Electronic music out of Essex. Proto industrial, electronic body music that crossed over into the acid house/Balearic mixes at the end of the 1980s. Best experience in a dank, sweaty, dark underground club where the bass is physical. Lyrics are a criticism of language and concepts used by fascist states.

Title: Join Our Death Cult
Comment: It was a tough decision between this, ‘Watch Evil Grow’ or ‘Suck My Mind’. An extremely fun band whose instructions are clearly worth following at all times.

Title: Stretch Your Eyes
Comment: A song about seeing beyond the surface appearances and questioning reality. An intimidating instruction for many people and relevant to the world we live in now. Instrumentation includes use of a Trautonium, a 100-year-old rare instrument with a cinematic and political history: https://spectrum.ieee.org/how-the-trautonium-found-favor-with-nazis-and-gave-hitchcocks-emthe-birdsem-its-distinctive-screech

Title: Dance with Me
Comment: Pleasantly surprised to see these guys haven’t been used yet. Had a chance to hang out with the lead singer Rhett Miller a few weeks back and I think I might have gotten a huge man crush. Super down to earth, friendly, engaging, and a man dedicated to his art. Lots of options from Rhett and the Old 97s but picked this one to shake off the soporific mood we have found ourselves in.

Title: We'll Meet Again
Comment: The meeting referred to in the title has not yet happened, but it will happen, at a time in the future (in another place, in another world), thus being eligible for this round. I have recently stumbled across the Lord Weird Slough Feg, who somewhat disappointingly have now dropped “The Lord Weird” from their name. They’re great aren’t they? I can’t imagine any of you will disagree.

Comment:

So instead, here's The Kills. I heard this in a shitty film I was watching last week, and unlike 2525, it only made me question my taste in cinema.

This is about that moment in the future when they see through your bullshit and figure you out - or maybe it’s more about the constant dread of that moment - or it’s about contorting yourself to make sure that you’re liked - or wait, is it actually about pretending to still have faith in God? Comment: Quincy Jones has a musical legacy that is wide ranging. Jazz,  blues, funk, producing.the biggest selling LP of all time. I am sure his personal career highlight was remixing Blue Monday 1988. This is from a year later and features one of the last recordings of Miles Davis.

Title: We Might Be Dead by Tomorrow
Album: I Thought I Was an Alien
Comment: First red-box! (Damn you people!) Nah... it's my own fault for a slow start. Anyway, my initial choice was high energy, gritty, and vaguely encouraging. This one is nearly the opposite in every way, quiet, delicate, and almost acquiescent in its assessment of the future. But, every rounds needs both yin and yang.

Title: Come Saturday
Album: The Pains of Being Pure at Heart

Comment: An American band combining the best bits of C86 and early 90's British indie pop as they wistfully look forward to the weekend and time with their loved one.  You're 80 miles away, Tuesday.

Title: Tomorrow Night
Comment:
When it comes to vintage power pop, few did it better than Shoes. Hailing from a small American Midwest town, the band fused their love of British Invasion music with the influence of Ziggy-era David Bowie, Todd Rundgren, and Big Star on several DIY recordings before signing with Elektra in 1978.

"Tomorrow Night" was originally released as a single before being reworked as the opening track on 1979's 'Present Tense', and remains a classic example of the genre.

Comment: “One night it will be summer”, that is obviously a night sometimes in the future. A bittersweet longing for something that has not arrived yet (but will in the future). It’s a band repeat, but there are only so many good Danish bands and you need to hear this melancholy song.

Title: Apocalypse Dreams
Comment:
Apocalypse—the end of the world. We don’t know exactly when in the future it will be. Probably before the sun burns out in five billion years? 

Think whatever you’d like about Mr. Kevin Parker, he’s probably thought it already himself. I recently read an interview on how he nearly binned 2015’s Currents because he thought it was too cheesy. Comment: For all you Nigerian R&B fans on this group (don't put your hands up all at once!) the lovely - and even in Nigeria quite unknown - Elo, with a sweet and soulful little tune.

Title: Latter Days
Album: How Long Do You Think It's Gonna Last?
Comment: Struggled with the theme and finding something new that we haven’t seen in the league yet. Having abandoned a Japanese disco track that just didn’t have enough juice I was scrolling through some of my recent favorite bands looking for related artists and stumbled upon Big Red Machine. BRM is sort of a rotating super group anchored by Justin Vernon of Bon Iver who you can’t miss on the chorus here, and Aaron Dessner from The National. Anaís Mitchell co-wrote and provides lead vocals on this track. Latter Days of course referring to the Last Days, which, at least in my life, I feel I have lived through at least 3 separate times.

Title: Je rêve
Comment:
Édouard Tremblay-Grenier is a rising Québécois musician and actor who started writing music at age 13 years. He is a multi-instrumentalist, with a style rooted in modern francophone indie pop, with a soft, introspective pulse. His debut album , _François Roberge_,  came out in January 2026 and introduces him as part of Quebec’s new wave of thoughtful, melodic storytellers. 

The final song on the album, “Je rêve” (“I dream”), is quiet, loving letter to his grandmother. His song is a grandson's lament, telling his grandmother of all the things he wishes she could experience and all the things he could do to try to help her. His one line "my name slips away from you, " let's us know he is losing grand-maman to dementia or Alzheimers. It's a beautiful ode, circling themes of love, longing, distance, memory, and family. It carries a hushed emotional gravity, and ultimately, the acceptance of the dying embers of a loved one's memory and life.

Title: Sleepyhead
Comment: Sleep prescribed as medicine by my favorite Boston Post-Hardcore band? Think I'll overdose.

Title: His Old Look
Comment: One common theme of Bongwater songs was setting Anne Magnuson's dream journals to music.  Well, manic free-flowing instrumentals befitting the energy of the confusing dreamstate.  This one is my favorite because she doesn't just recount the specifics of the dream, but helpfully adds in commentary that details the struggle for consciousness  ... as she's actively trying to rationalize these events and being pulled back and forth into the faux-reality of her mind.  Every time I listen to this song I hear something new.

Title: She Comes To Me In Dreams
Sleep
Comment: South London This Heat an odd mix of late prog, dub, jazz impro and early electronica and tape loops. This is the opening track off the bands second LP, one that has more "songs" on it.

Title: The Dream
Comment:
I had a dream, a dream I said
A bloody dream in which I said

Surprised we haven’t had Thee Oh Sees yet. Brilliantly described in their Spotify bio as ‘The Mamas and the Papas and Love run through a blender with bent and rusty blades’.

Title: Judy and the Dream of Horses
Comment: This is probably pretty well known in this group, but it fits the round perfectly (she's asleep when having the dream, it's not a metaphor) and is fantastic. In 2019 I went on the Boaty Weekender, a cruise round the Mediterranean with lots of bands curated by Belle and Sebastian. There was a pub quiz as part of this, which was won by a team made up mostly of members of Belle and Sebastian, which seemed a bit unfair as one of the rounds was on Belle and Sebastian. Our quiz team name was Judy and the Team of Arseholes. Coming up with the name is one of my proudest achievements in life.

Title: Dreams
Comment: Laurie Anderson and Kronos Quartet were both important for me when I started wandering down the paths beyond pop and rock, so I was pleased to see they'd collaborated on this project a few years ago - 8 years ago actually - based on her experience and losses in Hurricane Sandy. This track doesn't deal directly with that story (though thunder rumbles are included), but it does open with a very Laurie reflection on people talking about their dreams, which turns out to be a prelude to a story which walks the tightrope between dream and reality, full of Lynchian shifts of perspective and haunted sounds. As that kid said in the viral video "David After Dentist": is this real life?

Title: Nightmare
Comment: Mercyful Fate is a legendary early metal band, that many of the greats point to as inspiration. They are considered proto black metal and has inspired both thrash and death metal bands. Here is a song about literal nightmares.

Title: Iowa Dream
Comment:
Did you hear the one about the avant-garde cellist/composer who had sidelines in mutant disco, funk, country, pop and and folk songs?

Arthur Russell was a singular artist during his short lifetime, involved in far too many wide-ranging projects to list in this little box, so check out his Wikipedia entry.

He named this song "Iowa Dream", as it relays imagery and impressions from his boyhood in Iowa.  Was the genesis of it an actual nocturnal dream?  It is entirely possible!  We will never know for sure.  I am choosing to take his literal word for it and I hope you will, too.

Title: Asleep
Album: Sing Me to Sleep: Indie Lullabies
Comment: Let Amy Millan cozily ease you into sleep under a cover (GEDDIT?  Har har!).  Stars, first appearance, round 8 of our 8th league.  In numerology, the number 8 represents power, ambition, authority, and material or financial mastery.  Too bad max votes only go to 7.

Title: Silent Lucidity - Remastered 2003
Comment:
Visualize your dream
Record it in the present tense
Put it into a permanent form
If you persist in your efforts
You can achieve dream control

"The state of recognizing you are dreaming is known as lucid dreaming. In neuroscience terms, this happens when your capacity for metacognition comes back online. You’re able to examine your beliefs in the moment and assess whether the conclusions you’re drawing jibe with reality.

For the most part, we can't consciously choose what we dream about. But actively recognizing you are dreaming creates the opportunity for varying levels of dream control. 

Most people lucid dream just a few times in their lifetime, if at all. And even if they gain an awareness of their dream state, it’s even more rare to be able to actively control their dream content in real time."

https://www.brainfacts.org/thinking-sensing-and-behaving/sleep/2025/the-fascinating-neuroscience-of-lucid-dreaming-072325

Title: Talking In Your Sleep (2023 Remaster)
Comment: The definitive 80's anthem on somniloquy. While this song will be new to nobody, I honestly haven't heard it in ages, and it holds up. This is peak MTV.

Title: Dream Within a Dream
Comment:
Before he was a session keyboardist for bands like the Buggles, Krisma, and the Damned, Hans Zimmer grew up dreaming of becoming the next Ennio Morricone. And he essentially did. 

Then he was hired to make the score to Inception, an admittedly pretentious C. Nolan film about dream espionage. He hired Johnny Marr to play guitar to synth in Ennio style, and layered it with a tremendous slow-down of Edith Piaf’s iconic song to create the booming foghorn sound cinema fans will instantly recognize. 

Is this an Indie darling charming you with her wiles? No it is not. But JE NE REGRETTE RIEN!  (BOM BOMMMM)

Comment: A repeat offender artist I know but my musical taste pivoted after watching Pretty In Pink in the summer of 1986. I was clearly searching for something beyond chart pop but hadn't found it. Shellshock was a key that unlocked a whole new musical universe. New Order, The Smiths, Echo and The Bunnymen. My musical taste can be divided between pre and post buying the soundtrack.

Title: Nightcall
Comment:
This is another round that’s almost too wide open for my overthinking brain. But I’m traveling this week, so fortunately I don’t have time to go down that road. The movie Drive had a very specific style and atmosphere with a perfectly matched synth-heavy soundtrack. This song, which is arguably the theme track for the movie, perfectly captures the dark, rainy, intense, but controlled distance of the film. Normally, I’d go for something a little bit more bittersweet, as that’s my preferred mood, but those moments are a dime a dozen across film and TV. As far as a song and a movie being a matched set, this one is tough to beat.

PostScript: on the heels of the death of Glen Hansard, I also just saw a couple minutes ago that Kavinsky has passed away yesterday. This choice was not related to that news (I submitted the song on a couple days ago), but I am quite saddened by the loss of two unique talents this week.

Title: The Edge of Forever
Comment: Dream Academy’s “The Edge of Forever” pops up briefly in Ferris Bueller’s Day Off, and like a lot of John Hughes moments, it stuck with me. Growing up in a rural town where country and metal ruled, those soundtracks felt like secret doorways to something new. Even without an official soundtrack, one intriguing song could send me on a full-on hunt to find the song. That’s how I found Dream Academy's eponymous album on cassette on a trip to a nearby big city. I fell hard for it, soon on repeat play on my Tandy brand knockoff Walkman. Produced with the help of David Gilmour of Pink Floyd, the song itself feels cinematic. It perfectly brings the action packed day to a soft landing as Ferris and his girlfriend Sloane drift back to reality. The song lyrics questions the love an existing relation. In the film it quietly underscores the fact that Ferris and his pals are on the precipice of adulthood with big life changes ahead. The song feels timeless to me and remains a favorite.

Title: Cavatina (Theme from "The Deer Hunter") - 2010 Remastered Version
Comment: This song was written for The Deer Hunter-it was originally from a British movie called The Walking Stick...that movie and the original of the tune made famous by John Williams is worth investigation by itself. The Deer Hunter is a flawed masterpiece but maybe the better for it's more populist stance...the controversial Russian roulette scenes are obviously a metaphor for the pointlessness and random luck of war...I never saw the movie at the time but watched it many times on videotape in the 80's....the music fits perfectly as a follow on from the stark ending and plays as the characters are shown in flashback at their innocent peak.....the music evokes that sense of melancholy and sweet sadness of loss and time passing......whenever I hear it I stop what I'm doing

Title: Pruit Igoe
Comment: When I was 11 there was an audio/video store across the street from my local comic shop.  Every week I'd notice them showing off their high-end TV's in the window with a film showing a bewildering series of images.  I'd end up standing there entranced for 15 minutes at a clip trying to figure it out.  Finally I walked in and sheepishly asked a salesman about it, he kindly led me to a VCR and popped out a tape called Koyaanisqatsi.  As luck would have it PBS soon afterwards screened the film and I made my own tape copy, finally hearing the Philip Glass score that accompanied the visuals.  Since then it's been my favorite film ... though one that lacks actors, dialogue or a plot beyond what you, the viewer, brought to it.  This is the score to IMO the most stunning sequence, which details the end-result of a poorly planned St. Louis housing project.  I highly recommend putting the artist/song title in a YouTube search and listening to it that way rather than utilize Spotify.

Title: Overkill - Acoustic Version
Comment:
Colin Hay appears on one of my favorite sitcoms of all time Scrubs. Season 2 Episode aptly named “My Overkill”. Hay is credited as “Troubadour” in the episode seen throughout playing “Overkill”. He went on to appear 3 more times on the series. I had no idea he was out there as a solo artist until seeing this episode. Hay has credited the show with jumpstarting his solo career and introducing a new generation of fans to his work. His record “Man @ Work” was made possible from the interest generated by the show.

Title: Belle (Extrait de la série TV "Belle et Sébastien", 1965)
Album: Belle et Sébastien - Les grands moments de la série télé (Version originale)
Comment: I don't know how old i was, younger than 10 for sure. It was the  70s and UK children's television habitually included overdubbed European imports (including the frankly quite terrifying "The Singing Ringing Tree" - look it up young uns!). Clearly where B&S took their name from this was French  series about a boy and his Pyrenean mountain dog, Belle.  A series about solace in friendship, something I needed and yearned for at that time when I lived mainly in my own little world. I always remembered the theme song used to make me cry with its lovely melancholy pathos. Here it is.

Title: The Wise Man's Song (Original Theme from Small Prophets)
Album: The Wise Man's Song (Original Theme from Small Prophets)
Comment: I was making quite a list of movies and shows from decades past, then realised a great choice was sitting right in my lap. This is the theme song from Small Prophets, a BBC show from earlier this year, which I loved so much I watched it twice. The song plays at the end of each episode, so after 12 such listens, to me it's no longer just itself, it's also saturated with all the melancholic longing the characters go through across those episodes. Cinder Well is aka Amelia Baker, California-born and a devotee of Irish music who spent some years in County Clare, a dual influence that I think comes through in the dark glimmer of this song, which somehow works perfectly in the most English of shows.

Title: High Life
Album: Soul Jazz Records Presents DEUTSCHE ELEKTRONISCHE MUSIK: Experimental German Rock And Electronic Music 1972-83
Comment: Ibliss of course being one of the many names of the dark one. A groovy journey through the world of jazz/funk flutistry.

Title: Me and the Devil
Comment: A recent cover of Robert Johnson’s Me and The Devil Blues from the ‘30s, with chord structure borrowed from Gil Scott-Heron’s version. Lots of folklore about Johnson meeting the devil at a crossroads to sell his soul for mastery of blues guitar. Perhaps you’ve heard this version in the brilliant sci-fi series ‘Dark’ on Netflix, or as an appropriate background track to Jeffrey Epstein content online.

Title: No Lucifer
Comment: Starts off with a chant borrowed from British wrestler Big Daddy, then tumbles through a fever dream of images taking in 70s bikes, Sodom and Megiddo, tits and shit, and the eternal struggle between good and evil. Will it win? EASY! EASY! EASY! EASY!

Title: The Devil's Plaything
Comment:
Backworld is the recording projest of Joseph Budenholzer, an American neo-folk musician.  This is his duet with gothy singer Rose McDowall, formerly of Strawberry Switchblade (not to confused with gothy actress Rose McGowan, or gothy English golfer Ross McGowan).
In what I'm sure will be a change of pace from all the metal submitted in this round, this song features acoustic guitar and cello, as the lyrics vacillate between mystical transformation and romantic seduction.

Title: Devil Is Fine
Comment: Zeal & Ardor is what happens when talented people have too much spare time. Why did the slaves in America take on their slavemasters religion? That was stupid of them, they obviously should have worshipped the opposite deity. So Z&A came up with a musical mix of spirituals and black metal (the most satanic music ever) to envision another path taken (the left hand path). The result are some angry, vibrant albums, with a very peculiar mix of genres. This is less black metal than most of their songs, but their is some vague tremolo picking in the background at least.

Title: Satan
Comment: That's actually Satan playing the guitar, I reckon. And this is what he would sound like to me, not grandiose & alpha-male like in the movies, but quietly, weirdly creepy and reaching-for-your-soul threatening.

Title: Satan's a Woman
Album: Satan's a Woman / I Am a Witch
Comment: A timely selection!

Title: Dust Devil
Comment: At over 6 minutes that's plenty long enough to piss off you long song haters. And pissing people off was the Butthole Surfers' raison d'être. So that's all good then.

Title: The Devil in Mexico
Album: Who Will Survive, and What Will Be Left of Them?
Comment: This song is aptly described as cinematic. If you don't use that term, then you have to use a half dozen others as it seems to ramble across several genres and styles. Regardless, the atmosphere fits the subject matter with an air of unpredictable menace as both the music and lyrics shift from spare and plodding to noisy intensity. I can feel the shiver of the wide open night.

Title: Shit Sandwich
Comment:
Yes, they've been submitted before but, devil may care, I'm throwing caution out with the baby and the bathwater because they are one of my all time favorite bands and there's no chance of placing in the top 3. Yes today Satan!! 

I've spent many an evening seeing them play live in every decade since the 90s, so talented and so much fun to see live. Lead guitarist, Dave Busacker, a charming funny man, died suddenly of a heart attack in 2021. It was a devastating event for our community in the already terrible era of covid. They've regrouped after recovering from their loss and have an excellent guitarist now filling Dave's large shoes. At any rate, a highlight in every Pilgrims' show is when the audience is called upon to scream "Shit Sandwich!!" Never has that refrain echoed more true than right now. I'll be joyfully screaming just that when I see them play this weekend and with luck, I hope to be screaming " Shit Sandwich!" for at least two more decades. Viva Satan's Pilgrims!

Title: Diablo
Comment:
Know then, that after Lucifer from Heav'n fell with his flaming Legions through the Deep he landed in... Australia?!?

I know we've had a lot of Aussie music already, but I can't let Lasse have all the regional fun. "Diablo" is from the debut album by psychedelic rockers Mt. Mountain, and is a good encapsulation of the band's swirling sound. Theirs was a relatively short career, though, as they went on indefinite hiatus in 2022.

Better to reign in Perth than to serve in Heaven!

Title: Dancing With the Devil
Album: Pink Dogs on the Green Grass
Comment: Well, since we're supposed to be friendly with the devil why not have a dance?  I think with how meta today's youth are the art of a singer taking on a character during a song has largely been lost.  Nobody wants to get called out as a devil dancer.  Regardless, we do need a Canadian artist to meet our CanCon requirements and here he is.

Title: Hit Me, Satan
Comment: One of my oldest friends is a member of Spare Snare (although not on this album). Don’t let that stop you downvoting though. This is a bit of a deep cut (yes, they are all deep cuts to you) which I didn’t remember at all when I listened to it. It has some “interesting” vocal stylings which are not typical of the Snare. I think it’s pretty good.

Title: A Lost History
Comment: Bradford's Worriedaboutsatan. Calming, ambient electronica touching on similar themes of lost history to The Caretaker/Leyland James Kirby. The sound of the snow drifting past the fractured windows of the Overlook Hotel.

Title: Devil's Work
Comment: Miike Snow is actually a trio, and no relation to Takashi Miike, a Japanese auteur for the strong of stomach.  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miike_Snow

Title: The Devil's In the Details
Album: This Is It and I Am It and You Are It and So Is...
Comment: Ms Marnie Stern is from New York (New York!) and plays guitar in a high-speed finger-tapping style, ie. she's a shredder! Somehow, a female shredder is still a thing that some people find remarkable, and just to wrongfoot 'em even more, rather than singing in a rock-goddess smokes'n'bourbon snarl, she's more, er, well, you'll hear. Zach Hill (of Hella) takes up the challenge of hitting the kit fast enough to keep up with Marnie's dizzying runs. And the lyrics? Where we're going, we don't need lyrics. Oh wait, yes we do - they're a little unclear here and she's a little bit kooky, so here, knock yourself out: https://genius.com/Marnie-stern-the-devil-is-in-the-details-lyrics

Title: Runnin’ with the Devil
Album: Interpreting the Masters, Volume 2: (A Tribute to Van Halen)
